title: Core Systems Engineering
summary: The foundational course: hardware and concurrency through distributed systems, operating production systems, AI infrastructure, and staff-level skills.

levels.title: Start Here: Working With AI Agents

units.title: AI-Augmented Engineering: Leverage, Verification, and Governance
units.summary: How to use AI tooling autonomously and safely: delegation vs. ownership trade-offs, specification patterns agents can execute, repo setup for collaboration, verification as the bottleneck, context management, and playbooks for large teams, small teams, and solo projects. Candidate-ready for senior/staff roles and founding engineering.

units.title: Engineering Rigor at Speed: Spec-Driven Work, Tests, Evals and Pivots
units.summary: How to keep high engineering rigor while shipping quickly with AI tools: one feedback loop, spec-driven work, owning AI-written code, tests you can trust, evals for AI systems, agile pivots, precise rollouts and writing that scales.

levels.title: Thinking Tools: Frameworks for Problem Solving

units.title: Reasoning Under Constraints: Hardware Limits, Trade-offs, and Scaling Laws
units.summary: First principles: CPU cycles, memory hierarchy, Amdahl's law, roofline model. Why 2x resources ≠ 2x speedup. When is your bottleneck compute vs bandwidth vs network?

units.title: Systems Design Process & Communication
units.summary: The system design framework: requirements → constraints → architecture → bottleneck → scale. How to communicate your design decisions and handle clarifying questions.

units.title: Design Judgment: Trade-Off Frameworks & Decision Trees
units.summary: How to make sharp design choices: consistency vs availability (domain-specific), latency vs throughput (which lever first?), vertical vs horizontal scaling, caching strategy selection, hardware choices. Real decision trees for trading, AI-infrastructure, and cloud contexts.

units.title: Benchmarking: Statistical Rigor & Avoiding Pitfalls
units.summary: Warmup runs (discard cold cache/JIT), run N times (20-100), report percentiles (P50/P99/P99.9), avoid cherry-picking, confidence intervals. Measurement artifacts, CPU scaling, cache pollution. How to prove your optimization claim.

levels.title: The Machine: Hardware, Concurrency, Data Structures

units.title: OS Fundamentals: How a Machine Runs Your Program
units.summary: From zero: CPU, RAM, disk and caches; programs, processes, the kernel, system calls and file descriptors; threads, scheduling and context switches; virtual memory, page faults and out-of-memory kills; blocking and non-blocking I/O, the page cache and fsync; NUMA and when memory placement matters; files, directories, inodes and links; journals, atomic rename and what to do when a disk fills. Demos run on a Mac; Linux-only commands are marked as not run.

units.title: Concurrency Fundamentals: Locks, Atomics, Memory Ordering
units.summary: From zero: what a thread is, why shared state races, and the tools that fix it. Mutexes, semaphores and RW locks; atomics and compare-and-swap; why CPUs and compilers reorder and what memory ordering means; deadlock, livelock and priority inversion; production patterns (thread pools, bounded queues and backpressure, work stealing). Every demo is runnable on a Mac or Linux box.

units.title: Data Structures for Production: Hash Tables, Trees, Tradeoffs
units.summary: Hash tables: collision handling, load factor. B-trees, LSM trees, skiplists: when to use. Trade-offs for production. Benchmarking & measurement. Not just theory, but real-world choices.

units.title: Network Fundamentals - Connection Pooling, Backpressure, Congestion
units.summary: Advanced networking: connection pooling (managing scarce connections), backpressure (flow control), packet loss handling, congestion control. How networks actually work under load.

units.title: Network Protocols: From Sockets to TCP Latency
units.summary: From zero: IP addresses, ports, packets and sockets; how TCP delivers reliably and what its connection states mean; slow start and congestion control (why a new connection is slow); DNS, TLS and HTTP on the wire; CDN caching. Each idea has a command you can run.

units.title: Profiling & Bottleneck Finding - Tactics & Tools
units.summary: How to find where 1000ms actually goes. Profiling tools (perf, vtune, py-spy, flamegraph), reading results, interpreting bottlenecks. Production debugging techniques and common pitfalls.

units.title: Performance Engineering: Profiling, Benchmarking & Data Structures
units.summary: Profiling tools (perf, flamegraph, TSAN), benchmarking methodology, data structure choices (consistent hashing, bloom filters, skip lists). How to find and prove bottlenecks.

units.title: C++ Essentials: Performance, CUDA, and Interview Pitfalls
units.summary: Modern C++ for trading systems and AI inference: move semantics, RAII, CUDA fundamentals, cache locality, profiling, and common pitfalls.

units.title: Modern C++: Evolution, Features & Expertise Signals
units.summary: What is Modern C++? C++11 watershed moment onwards. Key features by release. Marquee features that signal expertise (move semantics, smart pointers, constexpr, concepts). Most effective for production code (RAII, ownership, compile-time guarantees). Interview prep for trading firms.

units.title: Memory Optimization: Quantization, Compression, Inference Efficiency
units.summary: Fitting 70B models on consumer GPUs: quantization (INT8, INT4), pruning, LoRA, distillation, memory-latency tradeoffs.

units.title: Lock-Free Systems: CAS, Memory Barriers & Correctness
units.summary: Compare-and-swap (CAS) primitives, memory barriers (acquire/release/sequential consistency), ABA problem, lock-free queues and stacks. Sub-microsecond trading systems.

units.title: Python Glue for Model Runtimes: Language Tour, Async, Profiling and Gotchas
units.summary: From zero, for a programmer new to Python: what differs from other languages (typing, defaults, packaging with uv, errors, context managers, generators, dataclasses, subprocess, logging); asyncio from what a coroutine is; profiling with timeit, cProfile and tracemalloc (py-spy described, not run); micro-batching, backpressure and graceful shutdown; and the traps that bite glue code, including what the GIL does and the free-threaded build. Every demo was run on a Mac.

units.title: Go for Systems: Goroutines, Channels, Context, GC, Common Gotchas
units.summary: Go runtime: goroutines and the scheduler, M:N threading, channels vs mutexes, context cancellation. Memory management: GC pauses, allocation efficiency. Common pitfalls: loop variable capture, nil interface, goroutine leaks, race conditions. Production systems in Go.

units.title: Rust for Systems: Async, Concurrency, Lock-Free Data Structures
units.summary: Rust for production systems: tokio, async/await, Arc/Mutex, lock-free channels, SPSC, memory safety guarantees at scale.

units.title: Database Fundamentals: Indexing, Sharding, Consistency
units.summary: B-tree/LSM indexing strategies, sharding patterns (range/hash/directory), consistency models (strong/eventual), transactions & isolation levels (ACID, CAP theorem). AWS scale.

units.title: Caching Strategies: LRU, LFU & ARC Eviction
units.summary: Cache eviction policies: LRU (temporal locality, simple), LFU (skewed workloads, cold item problem), ARC (adaptive, combines both). Real systems: Redis/Memcached (LRU), Netflix CDN (LFU), Java ConcurrentHashMap (W-TinyLFU).

units.title: API Design: REST vs gRPC vs GraphQL, Idempotency, Versioning
units.summary: REST, gRPC, GraphQL: tradeoffs. Idempotency keys, versioning, rate limiting. Pagination, filtering, error handling standards. Protocol design decisions. Common mistakes.

units.title: Message Queues: Semantics, Kafka & Lag
units.summary: Queue guarantees (at-least-once, exactly-once), idempotency keys, Kafka partitions, consumer groups, consumer lag, retention policy. AWS SQS/Kafka, stream processing, payment systems, audit trails.

units.title: Security Fundamentals: Auth, Encryption, Validation
units.summary: Authentication vs authorization. Encryption in transit vs at rest. Input validation & injection attacks. Common vulnerabilities. Not deep cryptography, but production security awareness. How to think about security in system design.

units.title: Cost Modeling for AI Inference - Economics & Tradeoffs
units.summary: Cost per token, cost-latency frontiers, and decision frameworks. How to estimate inference costs, when to trade latency for cost (smaller models, quantization, batching), and why cost thinking matters in production AI systems.

units.title: Frontend for Founders
units.summary: The founder-relevant frontend subset: rendering models and server components, state management, WebAssembly, and browser storage and offline behavior.

levels.title: Distributed Core: Consensus, Replication, Fault Tolerance

units.title: Distributed Systems Fundamentals
units.summary: Consensus algorithms (Raft, Paxos), network fundamentals (TCP, latency, packet loss). Foundation for all distributed system design.

units.title: Consistency Models: Strong, Eventual, Causal
units.summary: Strong consistency definition. Eventual consistency: what it means. Causal consistency. Read-your-writes. When to use which. Real-world implications. CAP theorem applied to actual problems.

units.title: Consensus Algorithms: Raft & Quorum Voting
units.summary: Consensus fundamentals: Byzantine generals, Raft leader election, log replication, split-brain prevention via quorum voting, recovery from network partitions. Real systems: etcd, Consul, CockroachDB.

units.title: Distributed Transactions - Coordinating Changes Across Services
units.summary: How systems coordinate changes across multiple databases or services. Two-phase commit (2PC) vs sagas vs event sourcing. ACID properties in distributed settings. Compensation logic, failure scenarios, and why dual-write fails. Outbox pattern for correctness.

units.title: Exactly-Once Semantics: Payment Systems, Idempotency, Deduplication
units.summary: What does 'exactly-once' mean? SQS FIFO + DynamoDB deduplication. End-to-end guarantees for payment systems.

units.title: Failure Modes & Resilience: Cascading, Byzantine, Partitions
units.summary: Why systems break under load: cascading failures, Byzantine failures, network partitions. How to detect and defend.

units.title: Fault Tolerance: Circuit Breakers & Rate Limiting
units.summary: Circuit breaker pattern (CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN), retry strategies (exponential backoff), rate limiting (token bucket, sliding window). Prevent cascading failures.

units.title: Load Balancing: Algorithms, Health Checks & Failover
units.summary: Load balancing algorithms (round-robin, least-loaded, consistent hashing), health checks vs graceful shutdown, fail-closed/fail-open, circuit breaker pattern, cascading failures. AWS, service mesh (Envoy/Istio), production reliability.

units.title: Stream Processing & Event Systems - Kafka, Windowing, Stateful Pipelines
units.summary: Stream processing fundamentals for data pipelines and real-time systems. Kafka architecture, partitioning, consumer groups. Windowing strategies, stateful processing, late data handling. Why streams matter for training data prep, real-time inference, event-driven architectures.

units.title: Control Plane and Data Plane: Desired State, Fleets and Failure
units.summary: From zero: how systems split deciding from doing, how desired state and reconciliation loops drive a fleet, how config reaches nodes and what they do when the control plane is gone, and how to review such a design.

units.title: Observability & Debugging: Instrumentation, Attribution, Production Tracing
units.summary: How to find the bottleneck in production: NVML, NCCL, flame graphs, distributed tracing. From latency spike to root cause.

units.title: Testing & Observability: When to Test, How to Measure
units.summary: Unit vs integration vs E2E: when to write each. Load testing, chaos engineering. Metrics vs logs vs traces. SLOs, SLIs, error budgets. Alert design, on-call automation. Production thinking for senior engineers.

units.title: Testing Distributed Systems: Determinism & Failure Injection
units.summary: Deterministic testing (controlled time, reproducibility), failure injection (network, Byzantine, timing), observability in tests, integration vs E2E patterns.

units.title: Deployment Strategies & Incident Response
units.summary: Blue-green, canary, rolling deployments. Feature flags. Incident response, blameless postmortems, severity classification, communication during incidents, root cause analysis. How to ship safely and respond to failures.

units.title: Failure Diagnosis: Root Cause Analysis Under Uncertainty
units.summary: Systematic methodology for diagnosing failures with incomplete data: latency spikes (lock contention vs GC vs network), memory vs CPU vs I/O contention, cascading failure detection, graceful degradation playbooks. Interview scenario: 'System is slow—diagnose in 5 min.'

units.title: SaaS Platform Engineering
units.summary: What enterprise buyers require before they sign: multi-tenancy and isolation, infrastructure as code, SOC 2 readiness, metering and billing, synthetic monitoring and SLOs.

levels.title: Design Synthesis: System Design Case Studies

units.title: System Design Case Studies: Archetypes & Prototypical Problems
units.summary: Canonical system designs firms actually test: order books (trading), inference servers (AI), payment adapters (fintech), caching & sharding (general SWE).

units.title: System Design Case Studies: Notifications, Search, Feed
units.summary: Notification system (push, email, in-app), distributed search indexing (1B+ documents), feed ranking (personalization, ML, cold start). AWS interview scale.

units.title: Infrastructure Primitives: Case Studies
units.summary: Deep dives into critical infrastructure components: key-value stores, distributed coordination, job scheduling, workflow engines. How to build the pieces that other systems depend on.

units.title: AWS Services for System Design
units.summary: DynamoDB schema design, SQS/SNS/EventBridge patterns, Lambda cold starts, S3 consistency, IAM in multi-tenant systems. Interview-focused for AWS/Stripe roles.

units.title: Design Communication: Thinking Out Loud Under Pressure
units.summary: Interview delivery skills: design red flags & smell tests, handling 'but what if X fails?' follow-ups, self-scoring mid-interview (are you over/under-selling?), ranking tradeoffs under challenge. Go from 'I have ideas' to 'I can defend them.'

units.title: ML Training Fundamentals
units.summary: Backpropagation and automatic differentiation, optimizers, learning rate schedules, batch size effects, data loading pipelines. The mechanics of training neural networks.

units.title: GPU Fundamentals: Architecture & Optimization
units.summary: From the intro level of neural-network-execution to the GPU itself: streaming multiprocessors, warps and divergence, the memory ladder and coalescing, the roofline (memory-bound versus compute-bound), occupancy, kernel fusion, why small kernels waste a GPU, streams and async copies, and how to read nvidia-smi. CPU analogues run on a Mac; CUDA and nvidia-smi commands are marked as not run.

units.title: LLM Inference Systems: vLLM & Sandboxing
units.summary: LLM serving at scale: PagedAttention memory, prefill/decode batching, continuous batching, Firecracker sandbox isolation. Real depth for inference-infrastructure roles.

units.title: Distributed Inference: Tensor Parallelism & Multi-GPU
units.summary: Multi-GPU scaling: tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, ring allreduce, data parallelism. Real communication costs and ring topology for 70B+ models.

units.title: AI Platform Orchestration: Kubernetes, Scheduling, Autoscaling
units.summary: Kubernetes essentials for AI workloads: pod/node scheduling, GPU device plugins, bin-packing, gang scheduling, inference autoscaling (queue depth, cold start, warm pools). Why GPU scheduling differs from CPU. Scaling models to zero and latency cost.

units.title: ML Evaluation Metrics - Choosing, Computing, and Improving
units.summary: How to measure if a model is "better". Precision, recall, F1, AUC, custom metrics. When to use each. How to detect when metrics don't capture reality. Crucial for ML infrastructure roles: evaluating new models, comparing architectures, proving improvement. Applies to tone-quality evaluation and general ML systems.

units.title: Data Pipeline Architecture - DAGs, Orchestration, Fault Tolerance
units.summary: How to build scalable data pipelines. DAG (directed acyclic graph) concept. Orchestration frameworks (Airflow, Dagster). Idempotency and exactly-once semantics for ETL. Fault tolerance and recovery. Why pipelines fail and how to prevent it.

units.title: Data Quality & Validation - Schema, Anomalies, Constraints
units.summary: Data quality as a first-class concern. Schema validation, constraint checking, anomaly detection. Drift detection and monitoring. Great data pipelines assume good data; building that assumption into the system.

units.title: Feature Stores - Centralized Feature Management
units.summary: Feature Stores as infrastructure for ML. Consistent features across train/serve. Real-time vs batch feature serving. Online and offline stores. Ecosystem tools (Feast, Tecton, Featureform). Reducing training-serving skew.

units.title: AI Skills for Senior SWEs
units.summary: 12-lesson deep dive into AI systems engineering. From mental models and agent architecture through production patterns (MCP, safety, RAG) to advanced systems skills (distributed training, unsafe code, team-scale adoption). Interview prep for trading, AI-infra, and systems roles.

units.title: Agent Systems Engineering
units.summary: Building a reliable multi-step LLM agent: planning loops, tool contracts, state and memory, retries and checkpoints, evaluation, guardrails, cost control and observability.

units.title: How Neural Networks Run: Tensors, Graphs, Kernels and Decoding
units.summary: From zero: what a neural network is as a program. Tensors and the forward pass, models as operator graphs, kernels and GPU memory, precision, transformers and the KV cache, and how to observe a model running. Every demo runs on a Mac.

units.title: Trading Systems: Market Data, Matching Engines, Backtesting, Risk
units.summary: Matching engine semantics, market data feeds (sequence gaps, snapshot recovery), order lifecycle. Backtesting pitfalls (lookahead, survivorship bias, data quality). PnL calculation, Greeks, risk metrics (VaR, Sharpe). Real-time systems constraints.

units.title: Latency Architecture: Order Books & Temporal Joins
units.summary: Sub-microsecond order matching and point-in-time correct temporal joins. Lock-free queues, memory pools, streaming alignment with Arrow. Interview prep for infrastructure roles (sandboxing and inference context).

units.title: Staff Engineering: Design, Trade-offs, and Leadership
units.summary: First principles for technical decision-making at scale: design documents and RFCs, build-vs-buy evaluation, error budgets and prioritization, leading without authority. How to drive decisions, build consensus, and manage complexity across organizations.

units.title: Founder Fundamentals: From Idea to Sustainable Unit Economics
units.summary: First principles: customer discovery, pricing models, AI unit economics, defensibility. How to validate problems, price products, and scale past unit economics cliffs.

units.title: Founder Engineering: Building Products & Platforms
units.summary: Technical decisions for founders: payments integration, auth systems, frontend architecture, infrastructure choices. Tradeoffs between DIY and outsource for early startups.

units.title: Founder Finance and Equity
units.summary: How equity and financing work for a technical founder: cap tables and dilution, SAFEs and priced rounds, option pools and vesting, liquidation preferences and exit waterfalls, equity taxes, term-sheet control, unit economics and runway, valuation and exit paths. General education; legal and tax lessons need a dated professional review.

units.title: Enterprise GTM for Technical Founders
units.summary: Selling to enterprises as a technical founder: paid pilots, pricing and packaging, security questionnaires and procurement, champions and sales cycles, contracts and SLAs, technical selling.

units.title: Hiring and Org Design
units.summary: Structuring interviews, leveling, hiring the first ten engineers, when to hire a manager, decision records and incident-driven culture.

units.title: Legal and IP Basics for Engineers
units.summary: Open-source licensing, employee and contractor IP assignment, MSAs and DPAs, and privacy-law basics. Educational only; each lesson needs a dated professional review.

units.title: Interview Execution: Patterns, Scoring, Real-Time Reasoning
units.summary: The missing piece: pattern recognition library (5 patterns solve 90% of problems), handling ambiguity in real time, time management in 45-min window, scoring yourself accurately (70 vs 85 vs 90), decision frameworks for incomplete information, war story analysis. How good candidates actually think under pressure.

units.title: Mock Interview Scenarios: Practice with Real Problems
units.summary: 30-min system design, 20-min debugging, 15-min reasoning problems with complete rubrics, probes, and time plans. Aligned to FIRM_SPECIFIC_INTERVIEW_RUBRICS.md.

title: Data-Plane and Inference Systems Engineer
summary: A focused order for a systems engineer who builds the data plane of an AI inference and workflow platform: working with AI tools while owning the result, Linux and profiling, networking and concurrency, Rust, C++ and Python, control-plane and data-plane design, how models execute and are served, and shipping into customer environments. Reuses core modules in the order that fits that job; the order is the author's judgment, not a measured result.
audience: Engineers preparing for senior systems roles on inference, workflow and data-plane platforms.

capstones.brief: Given a price or carbon time series and a queue of deferrable jobs with deadlines and power draw, schedule them to minimize cost or emissions. Evaluate against a naive baseline on held-out days and report where the savings vanish.

units.summary: Generation, transmission, distribution, frequency, balancing, reserves, and why supply and demand must match at every instant.

units.title: Cost Modeling for AI Inference - Economics & Tradeoffs
units.summary: Cost per token, cost-latency frontiers, and decision frameworks. How to estimate inference costs, when to trade latency for cost (smaller models, quantization, batching), and why cost thinking matters in production AI systems.

units.title: AI Platform Orchestration: Kubernetes, Scheduling, Autoscaling
units.summary: Kubernetes essentials for AI workloads: pod/node scheduling, GPU device plugins, bin-packing, gang scheduling, inference autoscaling (queue depth, cold start, warm pools). Why GPU scheduling differs from CPU. Scaling models to zero and latency cost.

units.title: Datacenter Power and Cooling
units.summary: Power delivery chain, backup, rack density, air versus liquid cooling, and how they bound what a site can host.

units.title: AI Load Profiles
units.summary: Training versus inference load shapes, ramping and synchronization, and how much of a workload is actually flexible.

units.title: Load and Price Forecasting
units.summary: Time-series methods for demand, generation, and price; evaluation that respects time; and the cost of being wrong.

units.title: Flexible and Grid-Aware Compute
units.summary: Shifting work in time and place using price and carbon signals, deadlines, and the reliability limits of doing so.

units.title: Data Pipeline Architecture - DAGs, Orchestration, Fault Tolerance
units.summary: How to build scalable data pipelines. DAG (directed acyclic graph) concept. Orchestration frameworks (Airflow, Dagster). Idempotency and exactly-once semantics for ETL. Fault tolerance and recovery. Why pipelines fail and how to prevent it.

units.title: Data Quality & Validation - Schema, Anomalies, Constraints
units.summary: Data quality as a first-class concern. Schema validation, constraint checking, anomaly detection. Drift detection and monitoring. Great data pipelines assume good data; building that assumption into the system.

units.title: Stream Processing & Event Systems - Kafka, Windowing, Stateful Pipelines
units.summary: Stream processing fundamentals for data pipelines and real-time systems. Kafka architecture, partitioning, consumer groups. Windowing strategies, stateful processing, late data handling. Why streams matter for training data prep, real-time inference, event-driven architectures.

title: Trading Systems & HFT Principles
summary: How electronic markets work and how trading systems are built and run: market microstructure, low-latency engineering, strategy families, execution, risk, and the infrastructure around research and backtesting. Reuses the core systems modules that matter most here and adds trading-specific depth over time.
audience: Engineers who want to build or interview for trading systems, from market data to risk.

capstones.title: Build a toy exchange and a market maker
capstones.brief: Implement a limit order book matching engine, replay a recorded or generated message stream, and run a simple quoting strategy against it. Report latency percentiles and PnL attribution, and explain what you would change for production.

units.title: Trading Systems: Market Data, Matching Engines, Backtesting, Risk
units.summary: Matching engine semantics, market data feeds (sequence gaps, snapshot recovery), order lifecycle. Backtesting pitfalls (lookahead, survivorship bias, data quality). PnL calculation, Greeks, risk metrics (VaR, Sharpe). Real-time systems constraints.

units.title: Market Microstructure
units.summary: Spreads, depth, queue position, tick size, auctions, adverse selection, and how the order book's shape shows up in strategy results.

units.title: Order Types, Venues, and Fees
units.summary: How orders are expressed and routed, how fees and rebates change behavior, and what market-structure rules mean for a system.

units.title: Latency Architecture: Order Books & Temporal Joins
units.summary: Sub-microsecond order matching and point-in-time correct temporal joins. Lock-free queues, memory pools, streaming alignment with Arrow. Interview prep for infrastructure roles (sandboxing and inference context).

units.title: Lock-Free Systems: CAS, Memory Barriers & Correctness
units.summary: Compare-and-swap (CAS) primitives, memory barriers (acquire/release/sequential consistency), ABA problem, lock-free queues and stacks. Sub-microsecond trading systems.

units.title: C++ Essentials: Performance, CUDA, and Interview Pitfalls
units.summary: Modern C++ for trading systems and AI inference: move semantics, RAII, CUDA fundamentals, cache locality, profiling, and common pitfalls.

units.title: Network Fundamentals - Connection Pooling, Backpressure, Congestion
units.summary: Advanced networking: connection pooling (managing scarce connections), backpressure (flow control), packet loss handling, congestion control. How networks actually work under load.

units.title: Time, Clocks, and Timestamping
units.summary: Clock synchronization, hardware timestamps, measuring tick-to-trade honestly, and where nanoseconds are lost.

units.title: Kernel Bypass and NIC Offload
units.summary: Why the kernel network path costs time, what bypass changes, and the trade-offs in operations and debugging.

units.title: Market Making
units.summary: Quoting, inventory risk, skew, adverse selection, and how latency and fees decide whether quoting pays.

units.title: Statistical Arbitrage
units.summary: Relative-value ideas, signal decay, costs and capacity, and the ways backtests fool you.

units.title: Execution Algorithms
units.summary: Slicing a large order: TWAP, VWAP, participation, implementation shortfall, and market impact.

units.title: The Research Process
units.summary: From idea to production signal: data hygiene, walk-forward testing, overfitting, and the review discipline around them.

units.title: Risk and Position Management
units.summary: Limits, exposures, PnL attribution, and how risk is computed in the hot path versus on the side.

units.title: Pre-Trade Controls and Kill Switches
units.summary: Fat-finger checks, rate and notional limits, circuit breakers for your own system, and how controls fail.

units.title: Failure Modes & Resilience: Cascading, Byzantine, Partitions
units.summary: Why systems break under load: cascading failures, Byzantine failures, network partitions. How to detect and defend.

units.title: Deployment Strategies & Incident Response
units.summary: Blue-green, canary, rolling deployments. Feature flags. Incident response, blameless postmortems, severity classification, communication during incidents, root cause analysis. How to ship safely and respond to failures.
